# Case studies

## Northwind Dashboard
URL: https://salahu01.github.io/quietfolio-template/work/northwind-dashboard
Published: September 12, 2026 · Personal · React, TypeScript, Node.js, PostgreSQL

> This is sample content that ships with the quietfolio template. Replace it with your own case study.

## Overview

Northwind Dashboard is a **sample** analytics app used to show how a case study page looks: a cover image, a short intro, headings, lists, code and a table, all rendered from `content/work.json`.

Good case studies answer three questions quickly: what was the problem, what did you build, and what changed because of it.

## The problem

Teams were exporting spreadsheets by hand every Monday. Numbers were stale by Tuesday and nobody trusted the totals.

## What I built

- **Live charts** — a typed API streams aggregates so the UI never recomputes them in the browser.
- **Role-based access** — admins see everything, viewers see only their team.
- **CSV export** — one click, the same numbers as the screen.

## A detail worth showing

Short code snippets render in a scrollable block. For example, the query that powers the weekly chart:

```
SELECT date_trunc('week', created_at) AS week, sum(amount) AS total
FROM orders
WHERE team_id = $1
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1;
```

## Results

| Metric | Before | After |
| Weekly report time | 2 hours | Instant |
| Dashboard load | 4.1 s | 0.9 s |
| Support tickets about totals | 12 / month | 0 |

## Links

See the [live demo](https://example.com) or read [how this template works](/blog/getting-started-with-quietfolio).

## Pocket Budget
URL: https://salahu01.github.io/quietfolio-template/work/pocket-budget
Published: June 3, 2025 · Personal · React Native, SQLite, TypeScript

## Overview

Pocket Budget is a **sample** mobile app. The goal: log an expense in under five seconds, even with no signal.

## The constraint that shapes everything

People log spending in shops, on trains and in lifts. So the app treats "offline" as the normal state: every write goes to a local SQLite database first and syncs later.

## How it works

1. Write the expense to local storage immediately.
2. Mark it as pending in a sync queue.
3. When a connection returns, push the queue and pull remote changes.
4. Resolve conflicts by last-write-wins per field.

## What I'd do differently

Conflict resolution by timestamp is simple but can drop edits made on two devices at once. A per-field vector clock would be the next step.

## Plainfile CLI
URL: https://salahu01.github.io/quietfolio-template/work/plainfile-cli
Published: February 20, 2025 · Open Source · Node.js, CLI, TypeScript

## Overview

Plainfile is a **sample** command-line tool that keeps folders of plain text files in sync, with a `--dry-run` mode so you can see changes before they happen.

## Usage

```
npm install -g plainfile
plainfile sync ./notes ./backup --dry-run
plainfile sync ./notes ./backup
```

## Design goals

- **Predictable** — the same inputs always produce the same result.
- **Reversible** — nothing is deleted without a confirmation or a backup.
- **Fast** — content hashes are cached between runs.

The source is on [GitHub](https://github.com/octocat/Hello-World).

# Blog

## Getting started with quietfolio
URL: https://salahu01.github.io/quietfolio-template/blog/getting-started-with-quietfolio
Published: October 1, 2026

quietfolio is a minimal developer portfolio template. It is a static Next.js site with a home page, case studies and a blog. This post is sample content that doubles as a setup guide.

## 1. Make it yours

Everything on the home page comes from `lib/data.ts`: your name, bio, links, projects, experience and tech stack. SEO defaults live in `lib/site.ts`.

## 2. Write content

Case studies live in `content/work.json` and posts in `content/blog.json`. Each entry has a slug, title, date and a list of blocks:

- `h2`, `h3` — headings
- `p` — paragraphs with **bold**, *italic*, `code` and [links](https://example.com)
- `ul`, `ol` — lists
- `quote`, `code`, `table`, `img`

Run `npm run validate` to catch broken links, missing images and duplicate slugs before you deploy.

## 3. Replace the images

Swap `public/img/avatar.jpeg` and the covers in `public/img/projects/`. The pixel-art banner is generated by `scripts/make_banner.py`.

## 4. Ship it

Read the [deployment guide](/blog/deploying-to-github-pages-or-netlify). Before you do, set `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` so canonical URLs and the sitemap are correct.

## How the SEO and AEO setup works
URL: https://salahu01.github.io/quietfolio-template/blog/how-the-seo-setup-works
Published: September 28, 2026

Search engines and AI answer engines both read the same signals: clean HTML, accurate metadata and structured data. quietfolio ships all of them by default.

## For search engines

- Per-page titles, descriptions and canonical URLs.
- Open Graph and Twitter cards, with a generated image for every post.
- A sitemap, `robots.txt`, RSS feed and web manifest.

## For answer engines

JSON-LD describes you as a `Person`, your pages as `TechArticle` and `BlogPosting`, and adds breadcrumbs. `/llms.txt` and `/llms-full.txt` give language models a clean Markdown view of the whole site.

## Checking it

After deploying, run a page through the Rich Results Test, submit the sitemap in Search Console, and run Lighthouse. The template scores 100 on SEO, accessibility and best practices out of the box.

## Deploying to GitHub Pages or Netlify
URL: https://salahu01.github.io/quietfolio-template/blog/deploying-to-github-pages-or-netlify
Published: September 25, 2026

quietfolio works on any host. There are two common setups.

## Netlify, Vercel or any Node host

Connect the repository and set `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` to your domain. Security headers and the content-security policy are applied in this mode.

## GitHub Pages

Pages serves static files, so the project builds a static export. One command does it:

```
npm run deploy:pages
```

That publishes to the `gh-pages` branch. Then enable Pages for that branch in the repository settings. Static hosts can't set custom headers, so prefer Netlify or Vercel for a production site.

## Before you go live

- Replace all sample content and images.
- Set your real email in `lib/data.ts`; it is also used for `security.txt`.
- Turn off the `NEXT_PUBLIC_NOINDEX` flag if this is your real site.
